title: Gunboat God sets November launch date for its crocodile-powered shoot 'em up
summary: Your mechanic in Gunboat God is a crocodile called Yeti. I’ve read that back a few times now and it still doesn’t make any more sense, but he’s apparently the best in the trade and a genuinely good guy, so I’ll stop asking questions. He’s heading to iOS and Android with the rest of this side-scrolling shoot ’em up, and to Switch as well. You’re stuck somewhere you don’t recognise, trying to get back to a Citadel in the sky, and the best thing you’ve got is a boat with an alarming amount of firepower bolted to it. Getting home means going through more than twenty mission types. Collision Course and Outlast explain themselves, while one is just called Boil. ... [MORE]

title: Old School RuneScape lets you test your mettle with the introduction of Hardcore Worlds
summary: Old School RuneScape and the whole RuneScape-verse has been going for nigh-on 20 years now, and for those looking for a challenge, there are plenty of bosses and dungeons to face. But now, even the most experienced of players can face a true trial, as today, Hardcore Worlds arrive in Old School RuneScape on all platforms, mobile included. Hardcore Worlds function exactly as you'd expect them to, but if you're new to the concept, here's a brief explainer: In Hardcore Worlds, death is final. As in no retries, no restarts. Whether it's slow or sudden, if your character perishes, you can either discard them or transfer them to a regular server, though without the rewards or goodies available exclusively on Hardcore Worlds. ... [MORE]

title: Monsta brings a turn-based portable classic to mobile, where it's you versus mutant monsters
summary: For many of us, the history of mobile gaming only stretches back to the first iPhone, and maybe a little further if we head back to the days of flip phones and the N-Gage. But look even further back, to when PDAs (Personal Digital Assistants) were all the craze, and you'll find examples of the primordial soup of mobile gaming, such as Monsta. First released back in the 2000s on PalmOS devices, and now available for the modern-day iOS and Android platforms, Monsta had to tackle many hardware limitations, including slow processing speed at the time. That's what inspired developer Superverse Industries to create this turn-based tactical shooter, where it's just you and a building full of monsters to get before they get you. ... [MORE]

title: Elder Scrolls: Sentinel has been named though not dated, but Elder Scrolls: Castles is here for a mobile fix
summary: Hallelujah! It seems that Bethesda Softworks have finally kicked themselves into gear, with the announcement that the hotly anticipated Elder Scrolls VI will be called Sentinel. And... Oh, turns out, that's all. Guess we're back to waiting, but if you need something to tide you over, did you know you can play The Elder Scrolls on mobile? Well, one of its spinoffs at the very least. With the shuttering of The Elder Scrolls: Blades earlier this year, options can seem thin on the ground. But dig a little deeper, and you'll find that Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls: Castles, which lets you build and manage your own fortress and family dynasty, offers you a hefty taste of Tamriel on the go!  ... [MORE]

title: Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra delays long-awaited major overhaul
summary: Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra, the 4v4 brawler that sees you and your friends pitted against other players as characters from Akira Toriyama's iconic manga, has delayed its hotly anticipated overhaul update. While originally scheduled for the end of the year, the patch has now been pushed back to March of 2027. Dragon Ball Gekishin Squadra's overhaul patch was set to make major changes, including a third-person camera perspective, simplified rulesets, and changes to both customisation and roles. While normal patches will keep rolling out, you'll have to wait a bit longer for the full overhaul to land. ... [MORE]

title: Gigabash Mobile brings arena-brawling action to phones with your favourite giant monsters
summary: Ever since Godzilla was stomping around Tokyo like a big playground, one question has been on everyone's mind: Let them fight. Alright, that's a statement, not a question, but my point stands. Big monsters are cool, so big monster versus big monster is even cooler, and that simple equation is exactly what Passion Republic Games' GigaBash Mobile is the solution to! In GigaBash Mobile, you're dropped into the open arena of a city, and made to fight against your fellow giant monsters to either save or doom humanity. That means duking it out between fully destructible environments, unleashing devastating attacks and generally laying waste to everything around you. ... [MORE]

summary: Guild Wars Reforged saw an MMORPG hit fondly remembered by many veteran players finally make a return. But, there's even bigger news on the horizon, as Guild Wars Reforged will also see the debut of the original Guild Wars' first DLC in over 20 years! Guild Wars Afterlife debuts January 13th 2027, with a suite of new content to enjoy. Guild Wars Afterlife offers a pretty stunning change of scenery too, with adventurers stepping through the Mists of Tyria and into the brand-new land of Xotecha. This South American-inspired jungle realm seems to be very different to what players of Guild Wars have experienced so far. ... [MORE]

title: The Spotter: Dig or Die challenges you to do just that in this roguelike tower defence
summary: In the post-apocalypse, everyone dreams of being the sole person to whom it falls to save everyone. Of course, no one anticipates all the work being the messiah requires, especially if it's just sticking in one place, maintaining a radio antenna. And what if that goes down? Well, as The Spotter: Dig or Die demonstrates, things can only get worse. The Spotter: Dig or Die sees you holding out against hordes of mutants on the edge of Las Veganos, awaiting a call from the President that could save the world. But when your station is buried under sand, it becomes a race against time to get things shipshape, while fighting off the hordes of mutants trying to take you down. ... [MORE]

summary: When I say 'roguelike deckbuilder', you say 'how high?' No, you don't actually, but we have another entry in this constantly growing genre to talk about! But things quickly take a turn for the worse as you'll need to battle different types of enemies across multiple environments in first-person, turn-based combat. ... [MORE]

title: Hill Climb Racing 2 gives you new adventure tracks, lore and more to celebrate ten years
summary: If you're a fan of wacky, physics-based racers, more than likely you've spent plenty of time with Fingersoft's Hill Climb Racing franchise. Now, you can celebrate ten years of Hill Climb Racing 2, one of their most popular releases, with an entire month of exciting in-game events for you to sink your teeth into, kicking off today! The celebrations in Hill Climb Racing 2 kick off with Adventure Week, which adds two new tracks, The Great Below and The Climb (no prizes for guessing what the gimmick of these tracks is). Shocking week follows right after, and promises both a new event type and 'special anniversary surprises' we're not yet privy to. All this, and a new mode too, but things don't stop there! ... [MORE]

title: Pokémon Go gets Gadget update, giving you easier hands-free collection
summary: While Pokémon Go is always a fun little ritual for those of us who want to get out of the house, sometimes you don't want to spend your time spinning PokéStops or catching Pokémon when you're rushing your way to work. For a long time, the Explorer Gadget has been the solution to that, and now it's getting a major overhaul! The Explorer Gadget will be familiar to all players over level 20 in Pokémon Go, as it's one of the primary 'AFK' tools for gathering rewards while you're out and about. Even with the screen locked, it will spin PokéStops and catch Pokémon. But now, there are additional functions that even let you use it while you have the app open! ... [MORE]

title: The Farmer Was Replaced brings its million-selling coding simulator to iOS and Android
summary: Consider this: a million copies sold of a game where you write code to run a farm. I wouldn’t have bet on that, but The Farmer Was Replaced got there, and it’s out now on iOS and Android with its new DLC, The Miner Was Replaced, thrown in. You write short programs in a Python-like language, hit execute, and a drone does the tilling, planting and harvesting based on whatever you wrote. No levels, just a steady run of unlocks and problems, like merging pumpkins into one giant one or hunting for treasure in a hedge maze. And if you already code, you can skip the basics and go straight to running a fleet of drones. ... [MORE]

title: Pokémon Go’s Twilight Wishes boosts Shiny odds and brings back Halloween costumed Pokémon
summary: A sky full of stars would be incomplete without boosted Shiny odds for Staryu and Elgyem. That’s Pokémon Go’s Twilight Wishes for you, an event landing later this month. It sees the in-game décor getting the starry treatment too. Wild encounters include Clefairy, Staryu, Elgyem and maybe a Rockruff, with Shiny versions possible across the lot. Raids are Pikachu in a sun crown or a moon crown at one star, Espeon in a sun scarf and Umbreon in a moon scarf at three, and Mega Beedrill, Houndoom, Sableye and Manectric at the top. ... [MORE]

title: Marvel Contest of Champions puts Doctor Doom in charge with its Empire of Doom Saga
summary: Doctor Doom taking over Marvel Contest of Champions’ fighting menu is the most Doom move. The Empire of Doom Saga takeover brings Latverian theming and monthly intro comics, with a motion comic for part one voiced by Matthew Mercer and part two landing in December, when the game turns 12. Star-Lord this time is Kitty Pryde, a comics swap that doesn’t sound real until you look into it. Peter stepped back as team leader, and she headed into space with the Guardians after falling out with the X-Men. Beast gets a rework, and the Victorious Four, a Fantastic Four who follow Doom without question, join the roster too. ... [MORE]

title: Bills Must Be Paid brings incremental, piggy bank-smashing gameplay to mobile, out now
summary: You know, it's a bit of a sad state of affairs that, while in the past video games gave us the fantasy of being skilled martial artists or world-defending space soldiers, nowadays it's just about making money. Well, at the very least, Bills Must be Paid is almost as visceral as the most violent boomer shooter, as it's now available to buy on iOS and Android! You may remember us covering Bills Must Be Paid a little while ago, but for those who don't, here's a quick primer. In Bills Must Be Paid, you have only one objective: smash piggy banks, get money and pay off your bills. To help you out, you'll be able to gain upgrades such as perks and rings, but watch out because you only have a limited well of stamina to draw from, and after that runs out, it's game over. ... summary: MiHoYo are stepping out of their comfort zone a bit with the upcoming Petit Planet, a cosy life sim where you take care of your own planetoid. And soon, you'll be able to get your hands on it and give it a go. Petit Planet has been confirmed to launch for iOS and Android on December 4th! Petit Planet sees you take on the role of a Tender, growing and expanding your own mini planetoid. You'll slowly gather a resource called Luca, and when you've created enough, you'll be able to add new life to your planet. Between building, planting, decorating and just enjoying life on your planet, you can explore the vast Starsea and go on adventures to other areas. ... [MORE]

title: Death Stranding Odradek shows us how Kojima's hit series might work on mobile
summary: Death Stranding is, for better or for worse, a quintessentially Kojima game. And it's found a lot of success on virtually every platform, including on mobile. But a newly released prototype app exclusive to a recent gallery could show how else the franchise works on mobile, as Death Stranding Odradek hits iOS and Android! Death Stranding Odradek allows visitors to the Azabudai Hills Gallery, which is hosting the 10th anniversary exhibition for Kojima Productions, to complete a delivery mission and experience the world of Death Stranding through AR. Odradek is named for the device worn on Sam's back in Death Stranding, which provides you with in-game information about the terrain and world around you, as well as warning of the presence of dangerous BTs. ... [MORE]

title: Dugout Dice turns baseball into a Balatro-style roguelike
summary: You can play any game with a die now. No, seriously. Dugout Dice has gone and done it to baseball, a sport that was mostly numbers to begin with. It’s out now on iOS, and every swing is a roll. You need to beat a target score before you hit three outs to get through each inning, then win enough games to make the playoffs and, eventually, a championship. Fall short at any point, and that’s your season done. ... [MORE]

title: Garena to premiere first episode of anime spinoff Free Fire: Daybreak at Brazil's CCXP26
summary: With all the news about gaming spinoffs, including PUBG Mobile getting an adaptation helmed by Donald Glover of all people, you'd be forgiven for forgetting about Garena's own Free Fire animated series. But it's just been announced that the first episode of Free Fire: Daybreak will debut at Brazil's CCXP26 convention! The series follows the characters Hayato, Moco and Kelly (the game's mascot) in an adventure set in New Dawn City. Controlled by the Horizon Corporation, there are mysteries afoot and a strange new power that'll aid our intrepid protagonists in breaking free of the constraints of society. ... [MORE]
